{{Quote|You're not in much of a position to object, are you, Solo?"<br />"Not in my ship. Not slaves. Never."<br />"You just think again, pilot. If you give me any trouble, you'll end up locked in a necklace yourself.|Zlarb and Han Solo|<ref name="hsr" />}}
'''Zlarb''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who helped lead a large-scale [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]] ring in the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]] during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Era]]. Originally a small-time organ trafficker, Zlarb entered into a slaving partnership with a [[Corporate Sector Authority/Legends|Corporate Sector Authority]] agent named [[Magg]] in [[6 BBY/Legends|6 BBY]], with Zlarb serving as the point man on the actual slaving runs themselves. After four prosperous [[Standard year/Legends|years]] in business together, Zlarb and Magg decided to get out of the slaving game in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], but not before making one last run to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Lur]]. However, their hired [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]], [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], were morally opposed to slavery, and Zlarb's attempt to force him to transport a load of slaves went horribly awry. Solo, Chewbacca, and his [[Droid/Legends|droids]] managed to overcome Zlarb and his slavers&mdash;in the chaos, one of Zlarb's [[Lurrian]] captives shot him in the chest, leaving him to [[Death/Legends|die]] on the floor of the ''[[Millennium Falcon/Legends|Millennium Falcon]]''{{'s}} cargo hold.

==Biography==
{{Quote|They told me you were a hard case, Solo. I see they were wrong. Those little beauties back there are worth four, five, maybe even six thousand apiece on the Invisible Market. They're natural-born experts at genetic manipulation, and in great demand, my friend. Not everyone is happy with the rigid restrictions that were imposed after the Clone Wars. It seems these creatures like their own world too much, though, and wouldn't sign out on contract labor for anything. So my associates and I rounded up a bunch. A few of them are sick or wounded, but we'll deliver at least fifty of them. I'll make enough off this run to keep me happy and lazy for a long time.|Zlarb, to Han Solo|<ref name="hsr" />}}
Zlarb's career in the criminal world started out at a relatively low station: as hired muscle for [[Ploovo Two-For-One]], a [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] based out of the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]]. It didn't take long for Ploovo to recognize that Zlarb had a type of business sense not usually seen in common thugs, and Zlarb soon found himself promoted to being one of the boss' [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]]. However, Zlarb was turned off by Ploovo's lack of ambition, and ultimately went into business on his own, leading a small-time organ-trafficking operation. That scheme got him on the radar of the [[Corporate Sector Authority/Legends|Corporate Sector Authority's]] [[Security Police/Legends|Security Police]], and in [[6 BBY/Legends|6 BBY]], an Espo agent named [[Magg]] hunted Zlarb down and arrested him. But while organ trafficking was a crime that could lead to the [[Death/Legends|death]] penalty, Magg surprised Zlarb by being more interested in talking business: the Espo wanted enter a partnership in a [[Slavery/Legends|slaving]] operation, as the two both agreed it carried with it the highest opportunities for profit. As a show of good faith, Magg even offered not to take a cut until they had reached a high enough profit level, convincing Zlarb to accept his deal.<ref name="hsc">''[[Han Solo and the Corporate Sector Sourcebook]]''</ref>

[[File:Magg.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Magg, Zlarb's longtime partner in slavery.]]
Although they might have seemed unlikely business partners, Zlarb and Magg had four profitable [[Standard year/Legends|years]] together. Zlarb did most of the dirty work, while Magg provided invaluable technical and logistical assistance, as well as using his contacts within the Security Police to make sure the heat stayed off their backs. A trained [[Malkite Poisoners|Malkite poisoner]], Zlarb used those skills to take out those who could prove to be obstacles, including once facilitating the [[Poison/Legends|poisoning]] of the [[Agmor Glayyd|Mor]] of [[Ammuud/Legends|Ammuud's]] [[House Glayyd]]&mdash;with whom Zlarb and Magg cleared most of their [[Starship/Legends|ships]]&mdash;when he threatened to leak information about their business dealings to the Corporate Sector Authority. By [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], however, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] had started to pay more attention to slavery, convincing Zlarb that it might be time to get out of the game. By that point, Zlarb and Magg had garnered sizable fortunes from their scheme, but Magg wanted to go on one final run to secure their retirement.<ref name="hsc" /> They settled on a run to the [[Water/Legends|icy]] planet [[Lur]], where Zlarb and a crew of several other slavers would seize a number of native [[Lurrian]] captives and catch a lift offworld&mdash;<ref name="hsr" /> although the slaving ring operated off of a retrofitted [[Dimel assault ship]] called the ''[[Eye of Shiblizar]]'',<ref name="hsc" /> the slavers used hired [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]], many of whom had no idea they'd be transporting slaves until they arrived, to carry their merchandise. From there, Zlarb and Magg would sell the Lurians on the [[Invisible Market]], where they could fetch up to a few thousand [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] apiece due to their natural ability as genetic coders.<ref name="hsr" />

On this occasion, however, the pilots Zlarb hired proved to be a bit too much to handle. Zlarb and his crew had little trouble taking a large number of Lurian captives, whom they had in [[Binders/Legends|chains]] by the time their hired ride&mdash;[[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and his [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] companion [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], who were promised 10,000 credits for their help&mdash;arrived on the [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] ''[[Millennium Falcon/Legends|Millennium Falcon]]''. Wielding a small [[palmgun]], Zlarb surprised the two pilots and commandeered their ship, threatening them with death if they didn't stay out of the way and take him and his men where they needed to go once the captives had been loaded into the hold. Zlarb and his crew quickly moved to secure the ship and restrain Solo's [[Droid/Legends|droids]], but made one mistake: they didn't account for [[Blue Max]], a small [[Computer probe/Legends|computer probe]] hiding in the chest cavity of Solo's [[Labor droid/Legends|labor droid]] [[BLX-5|Bollux]], which had been fitted with a [[Restraining bolt/Legends|restraining bolt]] by Zlarb's man [[Wadda]]. Linking itself into Bollux's motor systems, Blue Max managed to drive Bollux over to the ''Falcon''{{'s}} fire suppression systems, causing them to fire off randomly and throwing the ship into chaos. Zlarb was quickly set upon by Chewbacca, who knocked him unconscious before him and Solo went to free his cargo. The slaver revived in time to find Solo releasing the Lurrian captives, but his attempt at an ambush was snuffed out when one of the Lurrians [[Death/Legends|killed]] him with a [[Disruptor/Legends|disruptor]] shot to the chest.<ref name="hsr" />

Zlarb's body was disposed of by his surviving men, whom Solo handed over to the Lurrians to do with as they saw fit. The incident fueled Solo and Chewbacca to go on a personal quest to obtain the 10,000 credits he felt he was owed, and a [[Dataplaque/Legends|data plaque]] found on Zlarb's corpse pointed him towards [[Bonadan/Legends|Bonadan]], where he had planned to meet with Magg after the run. Their crusade resulted in the slaving ring's final dissolution, and Magg's [[Prison/Legends|imprisonment]] by the Corporate Sector Authority.<ref name="hsr" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Just play along and both of you will come through this alive.|Zlarb, to Han Solo|<ref name="hsr" />}}
A tall, broadly built man with a threatening and intense aura,<ref name="hsr" /> Zlarb was attracted to crime because, to him, it beat living an honest life&mdash;answering to a boss or working a back-breaking job was nothing compared to the money and freedom an outlaw's life afforded him.<ref name="hsc" /> And a life of crime suited him well: he was a cold-blooded and cocksure killer<ref name="hsr" /> with a sharp wit, a strong business sense and a driving ambition that led him to quickly make a name for himself in the criminal world. His partnership with the shrewd and duplicitous Magg thus proved to be a fruitful one, and while he sometimes resented having to do the dirty work, he recognized just how valuable the Security Police agent's contributions were to his organization's success. However, over time Zlarb grew cocky and assured in his continued prosperity,<ref name="hsc" /> and badly underestimated Han Solo and Chewbacca during his final run to Lur.<ref name="hsr" />

==Behind the scenes==
Zlarb first appeared in ''[[Han Solo's Revenge]]'', a novel written by [[Brian Daley]] and released in [[1979]].<ref name="hsr" /> He was later pictured for the first time by [[Mike Vilardi]] in [[1993]]'s ''[[Han Solo and the Corporate Sector Sourcebook]]''.<ref name="hsc" />

''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]'', published in [[1997]], incorrectly states that Zlarb and his men were subdued by Solo, Chewbacca and the Lurrians and not killed; subsequently, Zlarb and his henchmen were then bound in their own [[Shock collar/Legends|slaving collars]] and left in the hands of the [[Lurrian]]s.<ref name="EGWT">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>
